arxiv-1708-02527.title: Double-folding potentials from chiral effective field theory
arxiv-1708-02527.creator: V. Durant, P. Capel, L. Huth, A. B. Balantekin, A. Schwenk
arxiv-1708-02527.description: Abstract The determination of nucleus-nucleus potentials is important not only to describe the properties of the colliding system, but also to extract nuclear-structure information and for modelling nuclear reactions for astrophysics. We present the first determination of double-folding potentials based on chiral effective field theory at leading, next-to-leading, and next-to-next-to-leading order.

arxiv-2011-12926.title: No Stagnation Region Before the Heliopause at Voyager 1? Inferences From New Voyager 2 Results Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2011-12926.creator: A. C. Cummings, E. C. Stone, J. D. Richardson, B. C. Heikkila, N. Lal, J. Kóta
arxiv-2011-12926.description: Abstract We present anisotropy results for anomalous cosmic-ray (ACR) protons in the energy range ∼ \sim 0.5-35 MeV from Cosmic Ray Subsytem (CRS) data collected during calibration roll maneuvers for the magnetometer instrument when Voyager 2 (V2) was in the inner heliosheath.

arxiv-2101-06349.title: g-mode oscillations in hybrid stars: A tale of two sounds
arxiv-2101-06349.creator: Prashanth Jaikumar, Alexandra Semposki, Madappa Prakash, Constantinos Constantinou
arxiv-2101-06349.description: Abstract We study the principal core g g -mode oscillation in hybrid stars containing quark matter and find that they have an unusually large frequency range ( ≈ \approx 200 - 600 Hz) compared to ordinary neutron stars or self-bound quark stars of the same mass.

arxiv-2103-12311.creator: Hanwen Cao, Hao-Shu Fang, Wenhai Liu, Cewu Lu
arxiv-2103-12311.description: Abstract Suction is an important solution for the long-standing robotic grasping problem. Compared with other kinds of grasping, suction grasping is easier to represent and often more reliable in practice. Though preferred in many scenarios, it is not fully investigated and lacks sufficient training data and evaluation benchmarks.

arxiv-2104-10552.title: Preheating and Reheating after Standard Inflation
arxiv-2104-10552.creator: K. El Bourakadi
arxiv-2104-10552.description: Abstract We study the two-phase scenario following inflation, where the initial step is preheating, accompanied by a step of perturbative reheating at which inflaton field decays transferring all of its energy to create relativistic particles, the interaction of these particles will evolve towards a state of thermal equilibrium with a temperature T r ​ e T_{re} called the reheating temperature.

arxiv-2205-10176.title: Function-specific Scheduling Policies in Cloud-Edge, Multi-Region Serverless Systems
arxiv-2205-10176.creator: Giuseppe De Palma, Saverio Giallorenzo, Jacopo Mauro, Matteo Trentin, Gianluigi Zavattaro
arxiv-2205-10176.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Giuseppe De Palma, Saverio Giallorenzo, Jacopo Mauro, Matteo Trentin, Gianluigi Zavattaro. Cloud-edge serverless applications or serverless deployments spanning multiple regions introduce the need to govern the scheduling of functions to satisfy their functional constraints or avoid performance degradation. For instance, functions may require to be allocated to specific private (edge) nodes that have access to specialised resources or to nodes with low latency to access a certain database to decrease the overall latency of the application.

arxiv-2206-07593.title: HICEM: A High-Coverage Emotion Model for Artificial Emotional Intelligence
arxiv-2206-07593.creator: Benjamin Wortman, James Z. Wang
arxiv-2206-07593.description: Abstract As social robots and other intelligent machines enter the home, artificial emotional intelligence (AEI) is taking center stage to address users’ desire for deeper, more meaningful human-machine interaction. To accomplish such efficacious interaction, the next-generation AEI need comprehensive human emotion models for training.

arxiv-2305-15112.title: Random Sampling of Mellin Band-limited Signals
arxiv-2305-15112.creator: Shivam Bajpeyi Dhiraj Patel S. Sivananthan
arxiv-2305-15112.description: Abstract In this paper, we address the random sampling problem for the class of Mellin band-limited functions ℬ T \mathcal{B}_{T} which is concentrated on a bounded cube. It is established that any function in ℬ T \mathcal{B}_{T} can be approximated by an element in a finite-dimensional subspace of ℬ T . \mathcal{B}_{T}.

arxiv-2310-03500.title: Deep Generative Models of Music Expectation
arxiv-2310-03500.creator: Ninon Lizé Masclef, T. Anderson Keller
arxiv-2310-03500.description: Abstract A prominent theory of affective response to music revolves around the concepts of surprisal and expectation. In prior work, this idea has been operationalized in the form of probabilistic models of music which allow for precise computation of song (or note-by-note) probabilities, conditioned on a ‘training set’ of prior musical or cultural experiences.

arxiv-2411-05423.title: VISTA: Visual Integrated System for Tailored Automation in Math Problem Generation Using LLM
arxiv-2411-05423.creator: Jeongwoo Lee, Kwangsuk Park, Jihyeon Park
arxiv-2411-05423.description: Abstract Generating accurate and consistent visual aids is a critical challenge in mathematics education, where visual representations like geometric shapes and functions play a pivotal role in enhancing student comprehension. This paper introduces a novel multi-agent framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the creation of complex mathematical visualizations alongside coherent problem text.

arxiv-2503-22587.title: LLM-enabled Instance Model Generation
arxiv-2503-22587.creator: Fengjunjie Pan, Nenad Petrovic, Vahid Zolfaghari, Long Wen, Alois Knoll
arxiv-2503-22587.description: Abstract In the domain of model-based engineering, models are essential components that enable system design and analysis. Traditionally, the creation of these models has been a manual process requiring not only deep modeling expertise but also substantial domain knowledge of target systems. With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence, large language models (LLMs) show potential for automating model generation.

arxiv-2511-19669.title: HeaRT: A Hierarchical Circuit Reasoning Tree-Based Agentic Framework for AMS Design Optimization
arxiv-2511-19669.creator: Souradip Poddar 1 , Chia-Tung Ho 2 , Ziming Wei 1 , Weidong Cao 3 , Haoxing Ren 2 , David Z. Pan 1 1 ECE Department, The University of Texas at Austin 2 NVIDIA Corporation 3 The George Washington University {souradippddr1@, dpan@ece.}utexas.edu
arxiv-2511-19669.description: Abstract . Conventional AI-driven AMS design automation algorithms remain constrained by their reliance on high-quality datasets to capture underlying circuit behavior, coupled with poor transferability across architectures, and a lack of adaptive mechanisms. This work proposes HeaRT, a foundational reasoning engine for automation loops and a first step toward intelligent, adaptive, human-style design optimization.

arxiv-2511-20694.title: Reasoning With a Star: A Heliophysics Dataset and Benchmark for Agentic Scientific Reasoning
arxiv-2511-20694.creator: Kevin Lee, Russell Spiewak, James Walsh
arxiv-2511-20694.description: Abstract Scientific reasoning through Large Language Models in heliophysics involves more than just recalling facts: it requires incorporating physical assumptions, maintaining consistent units, and providing clear scientific formats through coordinated approaches. To address these challenges, we present Reasoning With a Star, a newly contributed heliophysics dataset applicable to reasoning; we also provide an initial benchmarking approach.

pmc-10672911.creator: Xinhu Liu, Yajun Zheng, Yanming Guo, Ningdong Hu, Hongping Hu, Aiqun Liu
pmc-10672911.description: As demand for haptic feedback increases, piezoelectric materials have become one of the best candidate materials due to their small size, high electromechanical coupling coefficient, and fast response. A stacked piezoelectric cymbal vibrator is proposed based on the common cymbal-type transducer, which is composed of a piezoelectric stack to drive and a cymbal disk to amplify displacement.

pmc-10736714.title: IDEA-EXECUTION ABILITY, SELF-DETERMINATION, AND CHEERFULNESS PREDICT DEMENTIA ONSET OVER NINE YEARS
pmc-10736714.creator: Yufang Tu, Teri Undem, Melissa O’Connor
pmc-10736714.description: The prevalence of dementia and its negative effect on well-being has made it a global public health concern. It is important to understand factors that predict the onset of dementia above and beyond age and physical health, to aid in preventative efforts.

pmc-11367119.title: Model-based prototype design, establishment and operation of ventilation system for underground gymnasium
pmc-11367119.creator: Ran Meng, Hui Li, Zhiyong Zhang, Chen Dong
pmc-11367119.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Underground small indoor gymnasiums (USIG) are important public places, it is vital to design and build a very economical and efficient ventilation system for effective closed-loop regulation of temperature and gases concentration at prescribed levels. In the article, the model-based prototype design, establishment and operation were proposed and applied to closed-loop control system of the underground small indoor gymnasiums’ ventilation system (USIGVS).

pmc-11513503.title: Standardized lab-scale production of the recombinant fusion protein HUG for the nanoscale analysis of bilirubin
pmc-11513503.creator: Paola Sist, Suman Saeed, Federica Tramer, Antonella Bandiera, Sabina Passamonti
pmc-11513503.description: The recombinant bifunctional protein HELP-UnaG (HUG) is a fusion product of the Human Elastin-like Polypeptide (HELP) with the bilirubin-binding fluorescent protein UnaG. HUG is used for the fluorometric detection of bilirubin in serum and a variety of biological fluids and extracts. Here we describe a detailed method for the standardized production and purification of HUG from E.

pmc-11644924.title: A Systematic Review of Cutting-Edge Radar Technologies: Applications for Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs)
pmc-11644924.creator: Can Ersü, Eduard Petlenkov, Karl Janson, Guangcai Sun
pmc-11644924.description: This systematic review evaluates the integration of advanced radar technologies into unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), focusing on their role in enhancing autonomy in defense, transportation, and exploration. A comprehensive search across IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, arXiv, and Scopus identified relevant studies from 2007 to 2024. The studies were screened, and 54 were selected for full analysis based on inclusion criteria.

pmc-11665279.title: Prevalence, Distribution and Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Enterobacteriaceae and Non‐Fermenting Gram‐Negative Bacilli Isolated From Environmental Samples in a Veterinary Clinical Hospital in Madrid, Spain
pmc-11665279.creator: Jesús Antonio Pérez Jiménez, Silvia Penelo Hidalgo, María‐Rosario Baquero Artigao, Gustavo Ortiz‐Díez, Tania Ayllón Santiago
pmc-11665279.description: Managing infections caused by multidrug‐resistant Gram‐negative bacilli is a major public health concern, particularly in hospitals where surfaces can act as reservoirs for resistant microorganisms. Identifying these bacteria in hospital environments is crucial for improving healthcare safety. This study aimed to analyse environmental samples from a veterinary hospital to identify prevalent microorganisms and detect antimicrobial resistance patterns.

pmc-11716649.creator: YUNYUN GUO, Shireen Sindi, Rui Wang, Lefkos T Middleton, Miia Kivipelto
pmc-11716649.description: BackgroundThe 2017 Lancet Commission on Dementia Prevention, Intervention and Care included air pollution in the list of potential risk factors for dementia. pmc-12609195.title: The Oral–Gut–Systemic Axis: Emerging Insights into Periodontitis, Microbiota Dysbiosis, and Systemic Disease Interplay
pmc-12609195.creator: Amani M Harrandah, Silvia Martu, Liliana-Georgeta Foia, Maria Alexandra Mârțu
pmc-12609195.description: The oral cavity harbors one of the most diverse microbial ecosystems in the human body, second only to the gut. Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease arising from oral microbiota dysbiosis, has been increasingly associated with systemic disorders such as diabetes mellitus, atherosclerosis, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and neurodegenerative conditions.

pmc-12630652.title: A Comprehensive Dataset of Factory Farms in California Compiled Using Computer Vision and Human Validation
pmc-12630652.creator: Varun Magesh, Nicolas Rothbacher, Saskia Comess, Erin Maneri, Kit Rodolfa, Sara Tartof, Joan Casey, Keeve Nachman, Daniel E. Ho
pmc-12630652.description: Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations (CAFOs) house livestock at high densities for prolonged periods of time, posing substantial risks to environmental and human health. However, limited public information on CAFOs has constrained efforts to quantify their impacts on proximate communities. Gaps in permitting and reporting have severely limited studies that rely primarily on administrative records.

pmc-12714161.title: Exploring the Role of Professional Burnout and Mental Health Strain in Nurses’ Turnover Intentions: A Mediation Study
pmc-12714161.creator: Ibrahim Abdullatif Ibrahim, Atallah Alenezi, Mennat Allah G. Abou Zeid, Mahmoud Abdelwahab Khedr, Ayman Mohamed El-Ashry, Bander Saad Albagawi, Samah Mohamed Abdelrahim
pmc-12714161.description: BackgroundNurses’ turnover intentions had a significant challenge to healthcare systems worldwide. Burnout substantially contributes to turnover intentions and actual departure behavior, yet the underlying mechanisms remain underexplored.AimTo examine the mediating role of mental health strain in the relationship between professional burnout and nurses’ turnover intentions.
